question: Ophthalmological ointments:

options.opa: They may contain solid particles but only with a controlled size.
options.opb: They do not need to be sterile.
options.opc: They require the test of pyrogens.
options.opd: They can not be W / O emulsions.
options.ope: Always your excipients must be fatty

analysis: Ophthalmological ointments are designed for application to the eye and must meet specific requirements to ensure safety and efficacy. They may contain solid particles, but these must be of a controlled size to avoid irritation or damage to the eye. Sterility is crucial for ophthalmic preparations to prevent infections, so they must be sterile. Pyrogen testing is typically not required for ophthalmic ointments, as pyrogens are more of a concern for injectable products. Ophthalmic ointments can be water-in-oil (W/O) emulsions, and while many excipients used are fatty to provide the necessary consistency and stability, it is not an absolute requirement that all excipients be fatty.
